parts:
Hello sirajum

I have been working on developing the MICAR and MPCAR models for Nimble and have a very inefficient

version currently. It uses the Jin etal LMC formulation. I interacted with Chris Paciorek about the efficiency and there are a number of fixes I need to make to

improve things. I can send it on once I have the fixes in place.

 

Meanwhile I should note that there is a multivaraite M model which was developed by Martinez-Beneito *

which is available for Nimble and WinBUGS.

An example of its use can be downloaded from the gitHub repository :

https://github.com/Andrew9Lawson/Bayesian-DM-code-examples

 

where you can fnd other Nimble Bayesian DM code examples.

 

I attach the Intrinsic code here also.

 

 

*Martinez-Beneito, M A; Botella-Rocamora, P; Banerjee, S. Towards a Multidimensional Approach to Bayesian Disease Mapping. Bayesian Analysis, 2017, 12, 239-259. Annex Material.

Botella-Rocamora, P; Martinez-Beneito, M A; Banerjee, S. A Unifying Modeling Framework for Highly Multivariate Disease Mapping. Statistics in Medicine, 2015, 34, 1548-1559. Annex material.

 

best wishes

Andrew

From: nimble...@googlegroups.com <nimble...@googlegroups.com> On Behalf Of Sirajum Munira
Sent: Tuesday, July 23, 2019 9:59 AM
To: nimble-users <nimble...@googlegroups.com>
Subject: Multivariate Spatial Poisson Lognormal Model

 

CAUTION: External

I am trying to develop a Multivariate Spatial Poisson Lognormal Model. I know Nimble doesn't have a mv.car function like winbugs does. I am wondering if there is any way to use the existing nimble function to develop the multivariate spatial model.

 

Here is my code

 

model {

  for (i in 1:Nint) {

    for (k in 1:Nsev) {

      Y[i, k] ~ dpois(mu[i, k])

      log(mu[i, k]) <- alpha[k] + beta1[k]*Vol[i] + beta2[k]*Sig[i] + S[k, i] + U[i, k]

    }                                                                         

    

    RR1[i] <- exp(alpha[1] + beta1[1]*Vol[i] + beta2[1]*Sig[i] + S[1, i] + U[i, 1])

    RR2[i] <- exp(alpha[2] + beta1[2]*Vol[i] + beta2[2]*Sig[i] + S[2, i] + U[i, 2])

    RR3[i] <- exp(alpha[3] + beta1[3]*Vol[i] + beta2[3]*Sig[i] + S[3, i] + U[i, 3])

  }

  

  # MV CAR prior for the spatial random effects

  S[1:Nsev, 1:Nint] ~ mv.car(adj[], weights[], num[], omega[ , ])

# MVCAR prior 

  for (i in 1:sumNumNeigh) { weights[i] <- 1 }

  

  for (k in 1:Nsev) {

    beta1[k] ~ dnorm(0.0, .0001)

    beta2[k] ~ dnorm(0.0, .0001)

    alpha[k] ~ dflat() 

  }

  

  # Bivariate normal prior for unstructured random effects within each area

  for (i in 1:Nint) {

    U[i, 1:Nsev] ~ dmnorm(zero[], tau[ , ])    # Unstructured multivariate normal

  }

  

  omega[1:Nsev, 1:Nsev] ~ dwish(R[ , ], Nsev)        # Precision matrix of MVCAR

  

  sigma2.s[1:Nsev, 1:Nsev] <- inverse(omega[ , ])

   #Covariance matrix of MVCAR

  

    

  # within-area conditional correlation between spatial components of variation 

    

  tau[1:Nsev, 1:Nsev] ~ dwish(Q[ , ], Nsev)       # Precision matrix of MV Normal

  sigma2.u[1:Nsev, 1:Nsev] <- inverse(tau[ , ])

     # Covariance matrix of MV Normal }

 

Thanks in advance

  

 

--

Hi Ben
my Nimble code for the MPCAR is given in the book Lawson, A. B (2021/2023) Using R for Bayesian Spatial and Spatio-temporal Health Modeling. This appeared in paperback in 2023. The simpler MICAR is also available. I attach a couple of txt files with code for MCAR and M-models ...see chapter 14 of the book. Also the site https://people.musc.edu/~abl6/ should have included code examples but I have just found out that it has broken links. I will fix soonest.

The MICAR/MPCAR  examples could be much improved no doubt.....I haven't had time to look further but would be very interested in any development or in testing new developments. Looking forward to seeing new code developments in this area.

best
Andrew
